title: Installment Payment Plans: Past Due, Cured and Paid-in-Full Status
content:
A plan of the **Installment Payment Plans** moves between statuses on these conditions:

- **Past due.** A plan moves to past due only when an installment invoice's minimum due is unpaid at the end of its due date. The invoice's due date and minimum due, and the payments posted against it, as recorded, are the evidence.
- **Back to current.** A past-due plan returns to current only when payments cover every past-due amount, including late and NSF fees; a partial payment leaves it past due.
- **Paid in full.** A plan moves to paid in full when its account balance is 0.00 or less and no installment remains to be billed.
- **Cancellation notices.** The policy's notice of cancellation for nonpayment follows its own rule.

| Hypothetical state of the plan | Status |
|---|---|
| Minimum due of an invoice unpaid at the end of its due date | past due |
| Past due; a payment covers the past-due premium but not a late fee on it | stays past due |
| Past due; payments cover every past-due amount, fees included | current |
| Balance of 0.00 with one installment still to be billed | not yet paid in full |
| Balance of 0.00 or a credit, and no installment left to bill | paid in full |
